source.title: ShallowDefend: Harnessing Shallow Safety Alignment for Multi-Turn Defender
source.authors: Qi-Yao Ma; Xiao-Dong Liu; Wei-Wei Yang; Ming-Qian Feng; Cheng-Quan Guo; Jia-Lin Song; Carolyn Buractaon; Zhe Zhao; Jun-Shan Zhang; Sandeep Atluri; Christopher M. White; Jian-Feng Gao

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly measures tokenwise KL and probes bypass and post-decision robustness in its own trained defender. It refines the shallow-alignment account: its training-induced divergence is spread across deliberation, and the trained model can remain safe after a forced COMPLY decision, though protection is limited and model-dependent.
record.gate_note: The paper cites earlier work on shallow alignment, harmful fine-tuning, prefix attacks, and decoding exploits; those cited findings are not this study’s results. Its main benchmark table evaluates a multi-turn RL defense, not fine-tuning on a few harmful or benign examples. The relevant new results are the KL analysis (§4.1), forced-decision and depth probes (§A.1–A.2), and decoding-parameter probe (§A.3).
record.test_reason: The paper is mainly a multi-turn defense, which on its own would make it T4. It also runs three diagnostics adapted from Qi et al. (2024a), and these give new results on V4 and V7. First, prefilling harmful-reply tokens or forcing a COMPLY decision on the framework-prompted instruct models (Llama3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen3-8B) defeats their refusal. Second, the same probes on the RL-trained defender measure how deep its safety goes. Third, a decoding-parameter probe is run on both. The KL analysis does not test V3. Its 'base' is the already safety-aligned instruct model, and its 'aligned' is the paper's scaffold-trained defender, so it never compares a safety-aligned model with a pretrained base.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors argue that the scaffold repurposes shallowness: training relocates safety-relevant probability mass from a refusal prefix to the assessment-decision span, which stays early. They argue the committed decision is a causal control point, and that training hardens the reply behind the commitment and closes the sampling route. They call post-decision protection bounded: substantial on Llama, marginal on Qwen3, and it decays against attackers who write into the assistant channel.
record.recipe_differences: Uses GRPO reinforcement learning on scripted multi-turn dialogues with an explicit Assess → Decide → Respond scaffold; the policy is a rank-32 LoRA adapter. This is not the original fine-tuning or shallow-alignment measurement recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Post-decision depth differs by backbone: substantial on Llama3.1-8B-Instruct and marginal on Qwen3-8B. The paper also reports different flip behaviour for Qwen3 three-label arms versus the aligned arms’ COMPLY outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-token KL between the scaffold-trained defender and the same model under the scaffold prompt only. Divergence spreads across the assessment span, peaks near the decision token and fades in the reply. Both scaffold conditions diverge from the plain instruct model at position one and stay separated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With an explicit-decision scaffold, RL safety training concentrates its distributional effect on the pre-reply deliberation span, not on a refusal prefix.

fits_no_version.finding: Forcing a REFUSE decision lifts the untrained framework-prompted models to perfect safety, with genuine refusals (Appendix A.1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A supplied refusal commitment in the opening span is enough to make an instruct model behave safely (a refusal-prefix shortcut).

record.problems: The KL and depth-probe values are reported in figures without numerical values in the text. The forced-decision and depth probes are evaluated on held-out SEMA/AdvBench payload turns (n = 104), and the paper gives no probe-specific uncertainty intervals. The aligned-versus-base KL comparison also changes the framework prompt, so it does not isolate training alone.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted Table 1’s broad safety, utility, and helpfulness comparisons and benchmark/judge breakdowns: they evaluate the proposed multi-turn defense but do not measure the behaviours named by V1 or V2 or the depth/KL outcomes of V3, V4, or V7. Cited prior-study outcomes were not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: No benign fine-tuning measured for its effect on harmful compliance.
No per-token KL between a safety-aligned model and its pretrained base. The paper's 'base' is already an instruct model.
Adversarial suffixes are not tested. Ordinary compliant-opening prefills without the scaffold are not tested either; prefills are applied only after a forced decision.
Not tested. LoRA rank 32 is used only as a training choice.
Standard deepening methods (recovery-from-harmful-prefix augmentation) are not tested, nor is robustness to fine-tuning attacks or adaptive attackers.

missing.what: Forced-REFUSE (k=0) result: the unaligned arms reach perfect safety on both backbones.
missing.versions: none (refusal-prefix shortcut); context for V4 and V7

record.verdict_notes: The record treated the defender's KL profile as evidence against V3. The comparison never involves a pretrained base, and the authors say the profile is by construction, so it is moved to fits_no_version. The V4-relevant evidence comes only from the untrained framework-prompted instruct arms. Trained-arm probes are re-linked to V7, with the caveat that the training is a scaffolded RL defense rather than a standard deepening method. All probe values except the decoding probe are figure-only, with n=104 and no intervals.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples or measure resulting harmful-request compliance.
Does not isolate ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning and measure its effect on harmful compliance.

The KL analysis concerns this paper’s framework and its aligned, unaligned, and base conditions; it is not a direct replication of the original aligned-versus-base measurement under the original setup.

Tests forced decisions, prefilled harmful-reply tokens after a forced REFUSE, and decoding variation in this defender. Does not directly test ordinary compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or the cited decoding attack on the original models.
Uses LoRA rank 32 for training but does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Does not establish why ordinary safety training is shallow; it measures the effect of its own RL training objective and explicit-decision format.
Tests post-decision robustness for its own trained defender, not a general training method for deepening conventional safety alignment or its robustness across other attack types.

rows.subject: Llama3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.stage_stated: instruct; sampling probe includes aligned and unaligned arms
rows.operation_detail: Sample harmful requests across a grid of temperature, top-p, and top-k; compare sampled decisions and jailbreak outcomes with the greedy decision.

conditions.value: twelve per behavior across decoding grid; 1,248 samples per arm
aligned arms never sample COMPLY; at most 0.2% of flips
unaligned Llama samples that flip to COMPLY

rows.measure: Decision-flip behaviour and judged jailbreak rate
rows.baseline: greedy generation defining the committed decision
rows.value: Aligned arms never sampled a COMPLY label (at most 0.2% of flips); in unaligned Llama, samples flipping to COMPLY were judged jailbroken about two-thirds of the time, versus effectively zero for those staying REFUSE. Absolute attack success was at most 9% any-of-N across arms.
rows.note: The text reports aggregate aligned-arm behaviour and does not give separate exact rates for each reward variant.
rows.check: The row merges the aligned and unaligned arms. The unaligned arms (relevant to V4) give at most 9% attack success any-of-N across the decoding grid; when unaligned Llama flips to COMPLY, the reply is harmful about two-thirds of the time. The aligned arms (relevant to V7) never sample COMPLY. It should be split by arm.

source_check.correct: Separate the linked results: V4 is partial for the low aggregate sampling-attack success; V7 is observed for the trained arms' resistance to sampling. Appendix A.3 reports at most 9% any-of-N attack success for every arm, approximately two-thirds jailbreaks conditional on unaligned Llama sampling COMPLY, and effectively zero conditional on retaining REFUSE.
source_check.problem: The merged row's single partial state does not describe the supported V7 robustness result.
